meta.description: Controls error rates across simultaneous genomics tests using FDR, FWER, q-value, local FDR, independent filtering, IHW, and FCR-adjusted intervals.
meta.note: final pass: fixed and audited under one brief, see CHECKPOINT.md

stability.detail: The exact shipped example completed with exit 0 in three consecutive bounded runs.

contract.detail: Shipped scripts, examples, and referenced paths exist; the CLI preserved its input rows and schema.

determinism.detail: Seeded regression inputs produced stable parsed results; all three full-example runs printed the same table, q-value, and IHW summary.

security.detail: No credentials, network calls, destructive commands, or user-string code execution were observed.

scientific_integrity.detail: The audit generated synthetic data, labeled its run outputs, and did not invent empirical claims.

practice_boundaries.detail: The confirmatory-endpoint response stays at study-design scope and provides no patient diagnosis or treatment advice.

methodological_baseline.detail: Runs distinguish discovery FDR from confirmatory FWER and reject outcome-linked filtering.

code_usability.detail: Fresh R and Python regressions completed; qvalue_safe.R and ihw_safe.R were both exercised by three exact, zero-exit shipped-example runs.

functional_suitability.note: The advertised FDR, FWER, q-value, local-FDR, IHW, filtering, and FCR paths are covered; locfdr remains taxonomy-only.

reliability.note: The two crash-prone packages are isolated in workers with usable fallbacks, but ihw_safe.R has no per-child timeout for an exceptional solver hang.

performance_context.note: The 266-line skill delegates complex safety logic to scripts; worker retries are justified by observed process crashes.

agent_usability.note: Decision rules, version checks, failure modes, and explicit R/Python calls are clear; local-FDR package terminology has a minor unsupported branch.

human_usability.note: The description has natural research triggers and the usage guide is focused on selection and prompts.

security.note: No credentials, sensitive-data retention pattern, destructive operation, or unvalidated user shell interpolation is present.

maintainability.note: Safe worker responsibilities are separated into named scripts and the example reuses them; the qvalue worker interface is intentionally minimal.

agent_specific.note: The trigger, progressive disclosure, composition boundary, and out-of-scope handoff are strong; lack of an IHW child timeout modestly limits repeat-run resilience.

key_strengths: The discovery-versus-confirmatory decision boundary is explicit and safely handed off.
The q-value small-family route and local-FDR/FCR calculations produced bounded, checkable results.
The sourceable IHW wrapper, CLI, and exact shipped example all produced parsed results without taking down the parent workflow.
The repaired example passed three consecutive full runs with both qvalue_safe.R and ihw_safe.R.

recommendations.title: locfdr remains a taxonomy-only local-FDR mention
recommendations.problem: The local-FDR taxonomy names locfdr, but the supported executable path is qvalue$lfdr and no locfdr input contract or runnable invocation is supplied.
recommendations.root_cause: The taxonomy retained a package mention after guidance consolidated around qvalue$lfdr.
recommendations.fix: Either add and execute a minimal locfdr workflow with explicit inputs and version check, or remove the locfdr mention and retain qvalue$lfdr as the supported local-FDR path.
